note: Arabic-script words compared in their own script (#92): after NFKC (which already turns presentation forms into letters), 'drop' marks are removed (vowel marks, shadda, sukun, superscript alef, tatweel, Quranic marks) and 'letters' are read as the letter given, so spellings that differ only by hamza seats, alef forms, ya and alef maqsura, ta marbuta and ha, the Persian and Urdu kaf, ya and heh, and Eastern Arabic digits compare equal. Read by the Rust port (create_token); .NET and Go hash it into the matcher version and will read it when they follow. Ranges are 'first-last' in hexadecimal. 'abdNames' are the names that follow Abd in Arabic names (the names of God, as romanised), so 'Abd al-Rahman', 'Abdel Rahman' and 'Abdulrahman' read alike while 'Abdul Karimov' stays a given name and a surname; Latin script, Rust only for now.
